A.explanation: The two equal forces are opposite and share the same line of action along the left edge, so resultant force and resultant moment are both zero.

B.explanation: The forces are opposite but offset to opposite sides, so they form a couple with a non-zero resultant moment and the object would rotate.

C.explanation: Both forces act upwards in the same direction, so the resultant force is twice one force and the object would accelerate upwards.

D.explanation: The downward and leftward forces are perpendicular, so their vector sum cannot be zero and the object would accelerate.

hints: Notice the two forces have the same magnitude and the weight is negligible, so only these two arrows matter for force balance.
Recall equilibrium needs both zero resultant force and zero resultant moment, so check direction and also whether the lines of action line up.
Compare diagrams A and B: both have opposite arrows, but only one has them acting along the same straight line with no turning effect.
walkthrough: Identify the given information: an isolated object with negligible weight acted on by only two coplanar forces of equal magnitude $F$.
State the rules for equilibrium: resultant force $\sum F = 0$ and resultant moment $\sum M = 0$ about any point.
Check resultant force: the two forces must be equal, opposite and parallel to cancel. This rules out C with two upward forces and D with perpendicular forces.
Check resultant moment: even if forces are opposite, if their lines of action are separated they produce a couple with moment $M = F \times d$.

In diagram B the upward force on the right and downward force on the left are separated by the width of the block, so $M \neq 0$. In diagram A both act along the left edge, so perpendicular distance $d = 0$ and $M = 0$.
Therefore both $\sum F = 0$ and $\sum M = 0$ are satisfied only in diagram A. This is option A.
